While leaders agreed on Pablo Hernández de Cos at the ECB, France and Germany pushed for a year-end deal to 'Le Pen-proof' the 2028–2034 budget—with French President Emmanuel Macron warning that ending Ukraine support would put Europe's security at risk and Paris requesting an extra €35 billion for farmers.

before.story: Labour MPs Revolt Against Proposed Rosebank Oilfield Approval
before.summary: Nearly 100 British Labour MPs and frontbench ministerial aides submitted a joint letter demanding that Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh block approval for the massive Rosebank oilfield off Shetland.

after.story: Labour MPs Revolt Against Proposed Rosebank Oilfield Approval

before.story: Dual Storms Threaten US Thanksgiving Travel
before.summary: Dual storm systems on both U.S. coasts—compounded by airline technical glitches and California high tides two or more feet above normal—have disrupted Thanksgiving travel, leaving more than 900,000 homes and businesses without power by Thursday evening and prompting San Francisco's mayor to urge residents to avoid non-essential travel. On the East Coast, 70 mph winds caused over 400 flight cancellations and knocked out power to nearly 200,000 customers in Virginia and 177,000 in Maryland.

after.story: Dual Storms Threaten US Thanksgiving Travel

On the East Coast, 70 mph winds caused over 400 flight cancellations and knocked out power to nearly 200,000 customers in Virginia and 177,000 in Maryland, while a king tide swept a man and his dog into the sea at Cannon Beach, Oregon.

note: Power outages approach 1 million; king tide sweeps man and dog into surf in Oregon

before.story: Spain Leaders Clash in Sole Pre-Election Debate
before.summary: Ahead of the November 29 snap election, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez teamed with Ada Colau against People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo and Vox's Santiago Abascal in a fiery debate dominated by housing affordability. Trailing by 0.7 percentage points, Sánchez banked on high turnout while overseas voting closed, marred by PP's controversial AI attack video.

after.story: Spain Leaders Clash in Sole Pre-Election Debate

Trailing by 0.7 percentage points, Sánchez banked on high turnout while overseas voting closed, marred by PP's controversial AI attack video and formal PP complaints to the Electoral Board over alleged irregularities in postal voting and propaganda distribution.

before.story: Australia Sanctions Iranian Operatives Over Antisemitic Arson Attacks
before.summary: Australia imposed targeted financial sanctions against two alleged Iranian agents accused of directing 2024 arson attacks on Jewish institutions in Sydney and Melbourne from overseas. The measures reflect heightened national security focus on foreign-backed violence and hate crimes.

after.story: Australia Sanctions Iranian Operatives Over Antisemitic Arson Attacks

before.story: Mexico Requests Extradition of Inés Gómez Mont From Spain
before.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed that television host Inés Gómez Mont was deported to Spain and announced a formal extradition request to bring her back to Mexico for trial. Sheinbaum publicly criticized U.S. authorities and Interpol after the international agency withdrew a red notice previously issued for Gómez Mont's arrest on fraud charges.

after.story: Mexico Requests Extradition of Inés Gómez Mont From Spain
after.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed that television host Inés Gómez Mont self-deported to Spain following an arrest by ICE and announced a formal extradition request to bring her back to Mexico for trial in a $150 million embezzlement case. Sheinbaum publicly criticized U.S. authorities and Interpol after the international agency withdrew a red notice previously issued for Gómez Mont's arrest.

note: Case involves $150 million embezzlement; Gómez Mont self-deported to Spain after ICE arrest

before.story: Makkah Pact Nations Convene as Turkey Ratifies Defense Deal
before.summary: Foreign and defense ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan convened in Islamabad for a two-day strategic summit on November 27–28 following Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's formal ratification of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in the Official Gazette. The emergency session addresses escalating regional instability triggered by Houthi missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and the Ras Tanura refinery, which drew retaliatory Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a.

after.story: Pakistan to Host Trilateral Defense Talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkey
after.summary: Foreign and defense ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan convened in Islamabad for a two-day strategic summit on November 27–28 following Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's formal ratification of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in the Official Gazette. The emergency session addresses regional security cooperation, defense manufacturing, and escalating instability triggered by Houthi missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and the Ras Tanura refinery, which drew retaliatory Saudi airstrikes on Sana'a.
